title: Major Test 01 - Chemistry Special 25Q Full Mock Test

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Ratio of solubilities of gases $\text{N}_2$ & $\text{O}_2$ in water from air at $25^\circ\text{C}$ & $1\text{ atm}$ will be if air is $20\%$ by volume of $\text{O}_2$ & $80\%$ by volume of $\text{N}_2$:

Given:
$K_H(\text{N}_2) = 2 \times 10^4\text{ atm}$
$K_H(\text{O}_2) = 10^4\text{ atm}$
questions.solution:
According to Henry's Law:
$p = K_H \cdot x$
where $p$ is the partial pressure of the gas, $K_H$ is Henry's law constant, and $x$ is the mole fraction (solubility) in water.

From Dalton's law of partial pressures at total pressure $P = 1\text{ atm}$:
$p_{\text{N}_2} = x_{\text{N}_2\text{ (air)}} \times P_{\text{total}} = 0.80 \times 1\text{ atm} = 0.8\text{ atm}$
$p_{\text{O}_2} = x_{\text{O}_2\text{ (air)}} \times P_{\text{total}} = 0.20 \times 1\text{ atm} = 0.2\text{ atm}$

Applying Henry's law for each gas:
$x_{\text{N}_2} = \frac{p_{\text{N}_2}}{K_H(\text{N}_2)} = \frac{0.8}{2 \times 10^4\text{ atm}} = 4 \times 10^{-5}$
$x_{\text{O}_2} = \frac{p_{\text{O}_2}}{K_H(\text{O}_2)} = \frac{0.2}{10^4\text{ atm}} = 2 \times 10^{-5}$

Ratio of solubilities $\frac{x_{\text{N}_2}}{x_{\text{O}_2}}$:
$$\frac{x_{\text{N}_2}}{x_{\text{O}_2}} = \frac{4 \times 10^{-5}}{2 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{2}{1} = 2 : 1$$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The resistance of $0.05\text{ M}$ solution of oxalic acid is $200\;\Omega$ and cell constant is $2.0\text{ cm}^{-1}$, the equivalent conductance (in $\text{S cm}^2\text{ eq}^{-1}$) of $0.05\text{ M}$ oxalic acid is:
questions.solution:
Specific conductance (conductivity, $\kappa$):
$$\kappa = \frac{1}{R} \times \left(\frac{l}{A}\right) = \frac{1}{200\;\Omega} \times 2.0\text{ cm}^{-1} = 10^{-2}\text{ S cm}^{-1}$$

Oxalic acid, $(\text{COOH})_2$, is a dibasic acid with $n$-factor = 2.
Normality ($N$) of $0.05\text{ M}$ oxalic acid solution:
$$N = \text{Molarity} \times n\text{-factor} = 0.05 \times 2 = 0.1\text{ N} = 0.1\text{ eq L}^{-1}$$

Equivalent conductance ($\Lambda_{eq}$):
$$\Lambda_{eq} = \frac{\kappa \times 1000}{N} = \frac{10^{-2} \times 1000}{0.1} = 100\text{ S cm}^2\text{ eq}^{-1}$$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The decomposition of a gaseous substance (A) to yield gaseous products (B) and (C) follows first order kinetics. If initially only (A) is present and 10 minutes after the start of the reaction, the pressure of (A) is $200\text{ mm Hg}$ and the total pressure is $300\text{ mm Hg}$, then the rate constant for reaction $A \rightarrow B + C$ is:
questions.solution:
For the first order reaction in gas phase:
$$\begin{array}{lccc}
& A(g) & \rightarrow & B(g) & + & C(g) \\
t = 0 & P_0 & & 0 & & 0 \\
t = 10\text{ min} & P_0 - x & & x & & x
\end{array}$$

Given:
Partial pressure of $A$ at $t = 10\text{ min}$:
$P_A = P_0 - x = 200\text{ mm Hg} \quad \text{--- (1)}$

Total pressure at $t = 10\text{ min}$:
$P_t = (P_0 - x) + x + x = P_0 + x = 300\text{ mm Hg} \quad \text{--- (2)}$

Adding (1) and (2):
$2P_0 = 500 \implies P_0 = 250\text{ mm Hg}$
$x = 300 - 250 = 50\text{ mm Hg}$

Rate constant $k$ with time in seconds ($t = 10\text{ min} = 600\text{ s}$):
$$k = \frac{1}{t} \ln\left(\frac{P_0}{P_0 - x}\right) = \frac{1}{600} \ln\left(\frac{250}{200}\right) = \frac{1}{600} \ln(1.25)\text{ sec}^{-1}$$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following reaction / statement is INCORRECT?
questions.option_d: Boric acid is polymeric due to the presence of hydrogen bonds
questions.solution:
(A) Correct: Due to the inert pair effect, the stability of the $+2$ oxidation state increases down Group 14: $\text{SiX}_2 < \text{GeX}_2 < \text{SnX}_2 < \text{PbX}_2$.

(B) Correct: In the Solvay process, ammonia reacts with carbon dioxide and water to produce ammonium carbonate: $2\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow (\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3$.

(C) INCORRECT: On heating washing soda ($\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}$), it loses water of crystallization to form monohydrate $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$ below $373\text{ K}$, and above $373\text{ K}$ becomes anhydrous sodium carbonate (soda ash, $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$). Alkali metal carbonates (except $\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3$) do not decompose to $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{CO}_2$ under normal heating due to high thermal stability.

(D) Correct: Orthoboric acid ($\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3$) forms a two-dimensional sheet layer structure where planar $\text{B(OH)}_3$ units are linked by hydrogen bonds.

Hence, the incorrect statement is (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: When $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas is passed in acidic medium (dil. $\text{HCl}$), which set of cations get precipitated?
questions.solution:
In qualitative inorganic salt analysis:
- Group II cations ($\text{Pb}^{2+}, \text{Cu}^{2+}, \text{Bi}^{3+}$) have very low solubility products ($K_{sp}$) for their sulphides.
- Dilute $\text{HCl}$ provides $\text{H}^+$ ions, which suppress the ionization of weak acid $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ via the common ion effect, keeping $[\text{S}^{2-}]$ very low.
- This low concentration of sulphide ions is sufficient to exceed the ionic product of sparingly soluble Group II sulphides ($\text{PbS}, \text{CuS}, \text{Bi}_2\text{S}_3$), precipitating them exclusively while Group IV cations ($\text{Mn}^{2+}, \text{Co}^{2+}, \text{Zn}^{2+}$) remain in solution.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: On heating compound X a gas Y is obtained, which is also manufactured by reaction of $\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2 + \text{Zn} + \text{KOH(aq.)}$. Which statement is correct regarding gas Y?
questions.option_b: Gas Y is used in Ostwald process
questions.option_c: Gas Y is colourless and odourless
questions.option_d: Gas Y produce blue solution in $\text{AgNO}_3\text{ (aq.)}$
questions.solution:
The reduction of nitrate ion by zinc in strongly alkaline medium yields ammonia gas ($\text{NH}_3$):
$$\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2 + 8\text{Zn} + 16\text{KOH} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3\uparrow + \text{Ba(OH)}_2 + 8\text{K}_2\text{ZnO}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Thus, gas Y is ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$).

- In the Ostwald process for the industrial manufacture of nitric acid ($\text{HNO}_3$), ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) is oxidized by air in the presence of $\text{Pt/Rh}$ gauge catalyst at $500\text{ K}$ and $9\text{ bar}$ to nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$):
$$4\text{NH}_3 + 5\text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Pt/Rh}} 4\text{NO} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
- Ammonia is colourless with a pungent, biting odour (not odourless).
- Heating $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ yields dinitrogen ($\text{N}_2$), not ammonia.

Hence, statement (B) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
The $\Delta H^\circ$ for the mutarotation of glucose in aqueous solution,
$$\alpha\text{--D--glucose (aq)} \rightarrow \beta\text{--D--glucose (aq)}$$
has been measured in a microcalorimeter and found to be $-1.16\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. The enthalpies of solution of the two forms of glucose have been determined to be:
$$\alpha\text{--D--glucose (s)} \rightarrow \alpha\text{--D--glucose (aq)}, \quad \Delta H^\circ = +10.72\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
$$\beta\text{--D--glucose (s)} \rightarrow \beta\text{--D--glucose (aq)}, \quad \Delta H^\circ = +4.68\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Calculate $\Delta H^\circ$ (in $\text{kJ/mol}$) for the mutarotation of solid $\alpha\text{--D--glucose}$ to solid $\beta\text{--D--glucose}$:
questions.solution:
Given thermochemical reactions:
(1) $\alpha\text{--D--glucose (aq)} \rightarrow \beta\text{--D--glucose (aq)}, \quad \Delta H_1^\circ = -1.16\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
(2) $\alpha\text{--D--glucose (s)} \rightarrow \alpha\text{--D--glucose (aq)}, \quad \Delta H_2^\circ = +10.72\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
(3) $\beta\text{--D--glucose (s)} \rightarrow \beta\text{--D--glucose (aq)}, \quad \Delta H_3^\circ = +4.68\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Target reaction:
$$\alpha\text{--D--glucose (s)} \rightarrow \beta\text{--D--glucose (s)}$$

According to Hess's Law:
$$\text{Target Reaction} = (2) + (1) - (3)$$
$$\Delta H^\circ = \Delta H_2^\circ + \Delta H_1^\circ - \Delta H_3^\circ$$
$$\Delta H^\circ = 10.72 + (-1.16) - 4.68 = 10.72 - 5.84 = +4.88\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Select the INCORRECT statement regarding $\text{KMnO}_4$ and $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$:
questions.option_a: Both act as oxidising agent in acidic medium
questions.option_c: $\text{O}_2$ is used in the preparation of both
questions.option_d: The central atom of the anion in both has $d^3s$ hybridisation
questions.solution:
In potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$), $\text{Mn}$ is in $+7$ oxidation state with electronic configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^0$. It has zero unpaired electrons and is DIAMAGNETIC.
In potassium dichromate ($\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$), $\text{Cr}$ is in $+6$ oxidation state with electronic configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^0$. It also has zero unpaired electrons and is DIAMAGNETIC.

Their deep colours ($\text{KMnO}_4$ purple-pink, $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ orange) are due to Charge Transfer Spectra (LMCT: Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer from oxide ligand to empty $d$-orbitals of the transition metal), not unpaired $d$-electrons.

Therefore, statement (B) ('Both are paramagnetic and coloured') is INCORRECT.
Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Select the CORRECT option regarding the formation of molecular orbitals from the linear combination of $1s-1s$ atomic orbitals shown in the potential energy curve:
questions.solution:
In Molecular Orbital Theory (LCAO method) for combination of two $1s$ atomic orbitals ($\psi_A$ and $\psi_B$):
1. Bonding Molecular Orbital (BMO):
Formed by constructive interference (addition of wavefunctions):
$$\psi_{(g)} = \psi_A + \psi_B$$
It has lower energy than the isolated atomic orbitals and exhibits a characteristic potential energy minimum (well) at the equilibrium bond distance, which corresponds to Curve-(2).

2. Antibonding Molecular Orbital (ABMO):
Formed by destructive interference (subtraction of wavefunctions):
$$\psi_{(u)} = \psi_A - \psi_B$$
It has a nodal plane between the two nuclei, higher energy than the isolated atomic orbitals, and is purely repulsive, which corresponds to Curve-(1).

Therefore, statement (C) is CORRECT: $\psi_{(g)} = \psi_A + \psi_B$.
Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For a $d^6$ metal ion in an octahedral crystal field, the correct electronic configuration is:
questions.solution:
In an octahedral coordination entity, the five $d$-orbitals split into lower energy $t_{2g}$ and higher energy $e_g$ orbitals with crystal field splitting energy $\Delta_o$.

For a $d^6$ transition metal ion:
- Strong-field condition ($\Delta_o > P$):
The energy required to promote an electron to $e_g$ is greater than the pairing energy $P$. Therefore, electrons pair up completely in the $t_{2g}$ set before occupying $e_g$, giving a low-spin configuration of $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$.
- Weak-field condition ($\Delta_o < P$):
Pairing energy is greater than crystal field splitting. Following Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity, electrons occupy $e_g$ singly after three electrons enter $t_{2g}$, yielding a high-spin configuration of $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.

Thus, the configuration $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$ occurs when $\Delta_o > P$.
Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text: Which one of the following order is NOT in accordance with the property stated against it?
questions.solution:
(A) Acidic strength of period 3 oxides increases across the period with increasing electronegativity and non-metallic character: $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 < \text{SiO}_2 < \text{P}_2\text{O}_5 < \text{SO}_3$. (Correct)

(B) For isoelectronic species (10 electrons each), ionic radius increases as nuclear charge $Z$ decreases: $\text{Al}^{3+} (Z=13) < \text{Mg}^{2+} (Z=12) < \text{Na}^+ (Z=11) < \text{F}^- (Z=9)$. (Correct)

(C) Nitrogen ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^3$) has an extraordinarily stable half-filled $2p^3$ subshell, whereas Oxygen ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^4$) has one electron pair in $2p$ experiencing interelectronic repulsion. Removing an electron from oxygen yields the stable half-filled $2p^3$ state. Consequently, the first ionization enthalpy of Nitrogen is greater than that of Oxygen:
$$\text{Actual } IE_1 \text{ order: } \text{B} < \text{C} < \text{O} < \text{N}$$
Thus, the given order $\text{B} < \text{C} < \text{N} < \text{O}$ is INCORRECT.

(D) Electron affinity order: $\text{Cl} > \text{F} > \text{Br} > \text{I}$, due to strong interelectronic repulsions in the compact $2p$ orbital of fluorine. (Correct)

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Both geometrical and optical isomerism are shown by:
questions.solution:
Analysis of coordination complexes:
- $[\text{Co(en)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ has the general formula $[M(AA)_2a_2]$:
  1. Geometrical isomerism: Exists as cis and trans isomers.
  2. Optical isomerism: The cis-isomer lacks any plane or centre of symmetry (chiral) and exists as non-superimposable mirror image enantiomers ($d$ and $l$). The trans-isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive.
  Therefore, $[\text{Co(en)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ exhibits BOTH geometrical and optical isomerism.

- $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+}$ ($[Ma_5b]$): Neither geometrical nor optical isomerism.
- $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^+$ ($[Ma_4b_2]$): Shows cis-trans geometrical isomerism, but both isomers have planes of symmetry and are optically inactive.
- $[\text{Cr(ox)}_3]^{3-}$ ($[M(AA)_3]$): Shows optical isomerism, but no geometrical isomerism.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In which of the following amino acids is a $2^\circ$-amino group present?
questions.solution:
Proline is unique among the 20 standard proteinogenic amino acids because its aliphatic side chain forms a 5-membered pyrrolidine ring by bonding back to the nitrogen atom of the amino group.
Consequently, its amino group is a secondary amino (imino) group ($-\text{NH}-$) rather than a primary amino group ($-\text{NH}_2$).

Glycine, Glutamine, and Phenylalanine all possess primary ($-1^\circ$) amino groups.
Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following compounds does NOT react with $\text{NaHCO}_3$?
questions.solution:
A compound reacts with sodium bicarbonate ($\text{NaHCO}_3$) to release carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) gas only if it is a stronger acid than carbonic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$, $pK_a \approx 6.35$).

- Acetic acid ($pK_a \approx 4.76$): $pK_a < 6.35$, decomposes $\text{NaHCO}_3$.
- Salicylic acid ($pK_a \approx 2.97$): Strongly acidic due to ortho-effect and intramolecular H-bonding, reacts readily with $\text{NaHCO}_3$.
- Squaric acid ($pK_a \approx 1.5$): Highly acidic because its conjugate dianion is aromatic ($2\pi$ electron system), reacts vigorously with $\text{NaHCO}_3$.
- Carbolic acid (Phenol, $pK_a \approx 10$): A weaker acid than $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$. Therefore, equilibrium lies completely to the left and it does NOT react with $\text{NaHCO}_3$ to liberate $\text{CO}_2$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What will be the correct IUPAC name for the following bicyclic compound shown in the structure?
questions.solution:
According to IUPAC nomenclature rules for bicycloalkanes:
1. The system consists of two bridgehead carbons connected by three bridges containing 3, 2, and 1 carbons respectively, giving the parent name bicyclo[3.2.1]octane.
2. The principal functional group is an alcohol ($-OH$), located on the 1-carbon bridge (C-8).
3. Numbering begins at a bridgehead carbon and travels along the longest path (3 carbons: C-2, C-3, C-4) to the second bridgehead (C-5), then along the second longest path (2 carbons: C-6, C-7) back to C-1, and finally through the shortest bridge (C-8).
4. Choosing the bridgehead carbon that provides the lowest locants for substituents assigns the methyl group to position 2 and the chloro group to position 7.
5. Listing substituents alphabetically gives:
7-Chloro-2-methylbicyclo[3.2.1]octan-8-ol.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the reaction shown below, 2-(2-chloroethyl)phenol is treated with sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) to yield product (P). Identify product (P):
questions.solution:
Reaction mechanism:
1. Acid-base deprotonation:
Sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) deprotonates the acidic phenolic $-OH$ group of 2-(2-chloroethyl)phenol to generate the phenoxide anion ($Ar-O^-$).

2. Intramolecular nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$):
The phenoxide oxygen attacks the terminal aliphatic carbon bearing the chloride leaving group ($-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$):
- Atom 1: Phenoxide oxygen
- Atom 2: Aromatic carbon with oxygen ($C_1$)
- Atom 3: Aromatic carbon with side chain ($C_2$)
- Atom 4: First aliphatic carbon ($-\text{CH}_2-$)
- Atom 5: Second aliphatic carbon ($-\text{CH}_2-$)

Ring closure forms a 5-membered cyclic ether fused to the benzene ring with displacement of $\text{Cl}^-$. Five-membered ring closure is kinetically extremely rapid.
The resulting bicyclic product is 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran (coumaran), which corresponds to structure (C).

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For the transformation shown below, which reagent(s) can be selectively used?
questions.solution:
In the transformation:
Reactant: Methyl 4-oxo-4-phenylbutanoate, which contains both a ketone group ($-C(=O)-$) and an ester group ($-CO_2Me$).
Product: Methyl 4-hydroxy-4-phenylbutanoate, in which the ketone has been selectively reduced to a secondary alcohol ($-CH(OH)-$), while the ester group ($-CO_2Me$) remains intact.

- Sodium borohydride ($\text{NaBH}_4$) is a selective mild reducing agent that readily reduces aldehydes and ketones to alcohols, but does NOT reduce esters under normal conditions.
- Lithium aluminium hydride ($\text{LiAlH}_4$) is a powerful reducing agent that reduces both the ketone and the ester group, producing a 1,4-diol.
- Catalytic hydrogenation ($\text{H}_2, \text{Raney Ni}$) may lead to over-reduction or hydrogenolysis of the benzylic alcohol.

Therefore, $\text{NaBH}_4$ is the appropriate selective reagent.
Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An antipyretic drug among the following is:
questions.solution:
Medicinal classification of the compounds:
- Paracetamol (4-acetamidophenol): An antipyretic (reduces elevated body temperature/fever) and analgesic (pain reliever).
- Seldane (Terfenadine): An antihistamine drug.
- Luminal (Phenobarbital): A barbiturate sedative/hypnotic.
- Aspartame: An artificial non-saccharide sweetener.

Therefore, Paracetamol is an antipyretic drug.
Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify which reaction(s) produce(s) a single optically active amine molecule as product:
questions.solution:
Evaluation of each reaction:

- Reaction (i):
The starting material is a piperidine ring with an unprotected secondary amine ($-\text{NH}-$) carrying an acidic hydrogen. Reaction with magnesium creates an organomagnesium reagent that is instantly quenched by proton transfer from the $-\text{NH}-$ group, destroying the Grignard species and precluding formation of a single optically active amine.

- Reaction (ii):
Electrophilic addition of $\text{HBr}$ followed by exhaustive catalytic reduction with $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$ at high temperature hydrogenates the ring and creates multiple chiral centres without enantioselective control, forming an optically inactive racemic/diastereomeric mixture.

- Reaction (iii):
Potassium phthalimide undergoes Gabriel phthalimide synthesis with an enantiopure chiral secondary alkyl halide ($(R)$ or $(S)$ 2-bromobutane) via an $S_N2$ mechanism with complete Walden inversion. Subsequent acid hydrolysis (dil. $\text{H}^+$) cleanly yields a single optically active enantiomer of $\text{sec}$-butylamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH(NH}_2)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$).

Thus, only reaction (iii) produces a single optically active amine molecule.
Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which one of the following carboxylic acids undergoes decarboxylation most readily on heating?
questions.solution:
Decarboxylation occurs most readily for $\beta$-keto carboxylic acids.

In $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{COOH}$ (acetoacetic acid, a $\beta$-keto acid):
1. The carbonyl oxygen at the $\beta$-position forms a cyclic 6-membered hydrogen-bonded transition state with the acidic carboxyl proton.
2. On mild heating ($100-150^\circ\text{C}$), concerted elimination of $\text{CO}_2$ occurs readily to give an enol intermediate ($\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)=CH}_2$), which immediately tautomerizes to acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$).
3. The development of carbanionic character in the transition state is strongly stabilized by enolate resonance with the adjacent $\beta$-carbonyl group.

Other keto-acids (such as $\alpha$-keto acid A, $\gamma$-keto acid B, $\delta$-keto acid D) do not possess a $\beta$-carbonyl group and cannot form this stable 6-membered cyclic transition state, requiring harsh pyrolytic conditions or sodalime for decarboxylation.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
For the complex $[\text{Pt(H}_2\text{O)(NH}_3)\text{Cl(Br)}]$:
If the oxidation number of $\text{Pt} = x$,
the coordination number of $\text{Pt} = y$,
and total possible geometrical isomers $= z$,
then find the sum of $(x + y + z)$.
questions.solution:
1. Oxidation state of $\text{Pt}$ ($x$):
Neutral ligands: $\text{H}_2\text{O} = 0$, $\text{NH}_3 = 0$.
Anionic ligands: $\text{Cl}^- = -1$, $\text{Br}^- = -1$.
Overall charge of complex $= 0$:
$$x + 0 + 0 + (-1) + (-1) = 0 \implies x = +2$$

2. Coordination number of $\text{Pt}$ ($y$):
All four ligands are monodentate.
Therefore, coordination number $y = 4$.

3. Total possible geometrical isomers ($z$):
$\text{Pt}^{2+}$ with $d^8$ configuration forms square planar complexes. For a square planar complex with four different monodentate ligands ($[Mabcd]$), keeping one ligand fixed and permuting the other three trans to it gives exactly 3 geometrical isomers:
- Isomer 1: $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ trans to $\text{NH}_3$
- Isomer 2: $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ trans to $\text{Cl}$
- Isomer 3: $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ trans to $\text{Br}$
Therefore, $z = 3$.

Sum:
$$x + y + z = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9$$

Hence, the correct answer is 9.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Experimentally it was found that a metal oxide has formula $\text{Fe}_{0.98}\text{O}$. Metal $\text{Fe}$ is present as $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ in its oxide. Percentage of the metal which exists as $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ would be (nearest integer):
questions.solution:
In $\text{Fe}_{0.98}\text{O}$, for every $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}^{2-}$ ions (total negative charge = $-2$), there are $0.98\text{ mol}$ of iron ions.

Let the fraction of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions be $a$.
Then the fraction of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions is $0.98 - a$.

By electrical neutrality of the ionic crystal:
$$\text{Total positive charge} = \text{Total negative charge}$$
$$2(0.98 - a) + 3(a) = 2$$
$$1.96 - 2a + 3a = 2$$
$$a = 2 - 1.96 = 0.04$$

Percentage of total iron existing as $\text{Fe}^{3+}$:
$$\%\text{ Fe}^{3+} = \left(\frac{0.04}{0.98}\right) \times 100 = \frac{4}{0.98} \approx 4.08\%$$

Rounding to the nearest integer gives 4.
Hence, the correct answer is 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 1 mole of monoatomic ideal gas is subjected to irreversible adiabatic expansion against constant external pressure of $1\text{ atm}$ starting from initial pressure of $5\text{ atm}$ and initial temperature of $300\text{ K}$ till the final pressure is $2\text{ atm}$. What is the final temperature (in $\text{K}$) in the process? (Take $R = 2\text{ cal mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
For an adiabatic process, heat exchanged $q = 0$.
From the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$$\Delta U = w$$
$$n C_v (T_2 - T_1) = -P_{ext} (V_2 - V_1)$$

For a monoatomic ideal gas, $C_v = \frac{3}{2}R$.
Using the ideal gas relation $V = \frac{n R T}{P}$:
$$n \left(\frac{3}{2}R\right)(T_2 - T_1) = -P_{ext} \left(\frac{n R T_2}{P_2} - \frac{n R T_1}{P_1}\right)$$

Cancelling $n R$ from both sides:
$$\frac{3}{2}(T_2 - T_1) = -P_{ext} \left(\frac{T_2}{P_2} - \frac{T_1}{P_1}\right)$$

Substituting the given values:
$T_1 = 300\text{ K}, \quad P_1 = 5\text{ atm}, \quad P_2 = 2\text{ atm}, \quad P_{ext} = 1\text{ atm}$

$$1.5(T_2 - 300) = -1 \left(\frac{T_2}{2} - \frac{300}{5}\right)$$
$$1.5 T_2 - 450 = -0.5 T_2 + 60$$
$$2 T_2 = 510$$
$$T_2 = 255\text{ K}$$

Hence, the final temperature is 255 K.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many of the following 11 alcohol compounds (A through K) will give immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent [anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2 / \text{conc. HCl}$] at room temperature?
questions.solution:
Lucas reagent (anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2 + \text{conc. HCl}$) reacts with alcohols via an $S_N1$ pathway involving carbocation formation:
- Alcohols yielding exceptionally stable carbocations ($3^\circ$, allylic, benzylic, dancing resonance, aromatic) react immediately, producing cloudiness/turbidity within seconds.
- Secondary ($2^\circ$) alcohols react within $5-10\text{ minutes}$.
- Primary ($1^\circ$) alcohols do not give turbidity at room temperature.

Evaluation of the 11 compounds:
1. (A) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{OH}$: Vinylic cation is extremely unstable $\rightarrow$ No turbidity.
2. (B) Cyclohex-2-en-1-ol: Allylic carbocation stabilized by resonance $\rightarrow$ Immediate turbidity.
3. (C) $\text{CH}_3-\text{OH}$: Primary alcohol $\rightarrow$ No turbidity at room temperature.
4. (D) Cyclopropylmethanol ($\text{c-C}_3\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$): Forms cyclopropylmethyl cation with extraordinary stability due to dancing resonance ($\sigma$-delocalization) $\rightarrow$ Immediate turbidity.
5. (E) Cyclopent-3-en-1-ol: Isolated $2^\circ$ alcohol, not allylic $\rightarrow$ Turbidity after $5-10\text{ min}$ (not immediate).
6. (F) Cyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-ol: Forms doubly allylic resonance-stabilized carbocation $\rightarrow$ Immediate turbidity.
7. (G) 1-Methylcyclohexane-1,4-diol: Contains a $3^\circ$ alcohol at C-1 $\rightarrow$ Forms stable $3^\circ$ carbocation $\rightarrow$ Immediate turbidity.
8. (H) Cyclopropanol: Highly strained secondary cyclopropyl cation $\rightarrow$ No immediate turbidity.
9. (I) Cyclohepta-2,4,6-trien-1-ol: Forms the aromatic tropylium cation ($6\pi$ electrons, aromatic) $\rightarrow$ Immediate turbidity.
10. (J) $\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$ (Allyl alcohol): Resonance-stabilized allylic carbocation $\rightarrow$ Immediate turbidity.
11. (K) $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{OH}$ (tert-butanol): $3^\circ$ alcohol, forms stable $3^\circ$ carbocation $\rightarrow$ Immediate turbidity.

Total compounds giving immediate turbidity: (B), (D), (F), (G), (I), (J), (K) = 7.
Hence, the correct answer is 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following compounds give a positive Prussian blue test for nitrogen in Lassaigne's test?

(i) Hydrazine ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$)
(ii) Ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$)
(iii) Ethanamide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2$)
(iv) Aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$)
(v) Hydroxylamine ($\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$)
questions.solution:
In Lassaigne's test for nitrogen, the organic compound is fused with metallic sodium. Carbon and nitrogen present in the compound combine with sodium to form sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$):
$$\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{NaCN}$$
When the sodium fusion extract is treated with ferrous sulphate ($\text{FeSO}_4$), boiled, and acidified with ferric chloride ($\text{FeCl}_3$), Prussian blue (ferric ferrocyanide, $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3$) is formed.

A positive test requires BOTH Carbon and Nitrogen atoms in the same molecule:
1. (i) Hydrazine ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$): Contains nitrogen but NO carbon. It decomposes on heating with sodium to yield $\text{NH}_3$ and cannot form $\text{NaCN}$ $\rightarrow$ Negative test.
2. (ii) Ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$): Contains carbon and oxygen but NO nitrogen $\rightarrow$ Negative test.
3. (iii) Ethanamide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2$): Contains both carbon and nitrogen $\rightarrow$ Readily forms $\text{NaCN}$ $\rightarrow$ POSITIVE test.
4. (iv) Aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$): Contains both carbon and nitrogen $\rightarrow$ Readily forms $\text{NaCN}$ $\rightarrow$ POSITIVE test.
5. (v) Hydroxylamine ($\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$): Contains nitrogen but NO carbon $\rightarrow$ Negative test.

Therefore, exactly 2 compounds (Ethanamide and Aniline) give a positive Lassaigne's test for nitrogen.
Hence, the correct answer is 2.
